assumptions: Local Git history of this repository contains merged PRs whose tests fail at the parent commit and pass at the merge commit. The SPEC-049 harness_verification partitions and D1-D3 rules stay as merged. SPEC-084 will provide a venue for the exploit agent; if not, tasks stay qa-incomplete. Infra-error classes can be decided from recorded logs by a rule frozen before data.
compatibility: Additive: new experimental schemas and modules; SPEC-049 discovery and holdout partitions keep their meaning and private-holdout is added only with owner approval; frozen SPEC-049 records, D1-D3 and the T005 roster unchanged. Rollback by reverting the change.
domain: Formats and procedures for a 20-50 task corpus derived from this repository's merged-PR history and the SPEC-049 lineages L1-L4, its per-task QA, and the trial-record rules for infrastructure errors, pinned configuration and run ids.
execution_contract: None. executionAuthorization is false on every record; nothing here runs an agent, model or container. The exploit-agent check runs only under SPEC-084 after its gates.
hypotheses: H1: this repository's history yields at least 20 tasks that pass the oracle, no-op, exploit and review checks. A lower yield is a valid feasibility result.
observation_contract: What task records, QA records, review records and trial records state, with their hashes; hashes bind bytes, not authenticity; review records are labeled human or model; a canary is a detection aid, not a contamination guarantee.

requirements.text: Task record format. Each task has a versioned record: id, origin (`repository-history` or `synthetic`), lineage, stratum (closed vocabulary, OD-2), family, source provenance, rights basis, initial-state commit, task statement, oracle (fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass tests), reference-solution hash, resource budget, canary id, partition, QA status (`pending`, `qa-incomplete`, `qa-passed`, `rejected` or `withdrawn`) and the SHA-256 of each file. Unknown keys refuse. Origin is a closed vocabulary: any other value refuses. Provenance depends on origin. A `repository-history` task records the PR number, pre-fix and fix commits and merge date. A `synthetic` task records its SPEC-049 case ids, its lineage id and the path and hash of the frozen SPEC-049 record it comes from. A field that does not apply to the origin holds the explicit value `not-applicable`, and each origin is validated against its own field set.

scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record: command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits. Planned path: specs/082-harness-task-qa-infra-controls/evidence/t005-inventory.json.

requirements.text: Selection rule before construction. The rule that admits a candidate from history is frozen by hash before any task is built. Every candidate, exclusion and its reason, and the observed yield are recorded. The rule fixes how a fix's test is checked on the pre-fix state: the fix's test and fixture changes, selected by a frozen path rule, are applied onto the parent tree without the code change. The candidate qualifies only when the changed test then fails and passes at the merge commit. Each failure is classified (assertion, error raised from code under test, collection or setup error), and the rule names which classes count; a collection or setup error of the test itself never does. Tests that need the network, a native host or a skip condition are excluded.

scenarios.when: a lineage spans two partitions, L1 is split, L3 is assigned, or a partition changes after any outcome record

requirements.text: Lineage and partition. Tasks that share a fixing PR, a spec feature, a test fixture base or an unresolved relation share a lineage (OD-2). A shared spec feature is a change under the same `specs/NNN-*` directory or a PR title naming the same SPEC number. A shared fixture base is a change to the same test module or the same fixture file under `tests/`. Each relation is an edge with its evidence; a lineage is a connected component of that graph (transitive closure). A pair whose relation cannot be decided is recorded as unresolved and merged. Partitions (`discovery`, `holdout`, `private-holdout`) are assigned by lineage, stratified, with a recorded seed, before any candidate outcome exists. SPEC-049 D1 holds: L1 is never split, L3 stays unassigned until resolved, L4 is held out only if it qualifies.

requirements.text: Private held-out split. Private task bytes live outside the public repository (OD-3). The public manifest holds only salted commitments (SHA-256 over a per-corpus secret salt kept in the private store, followed by the file bytes), counts and strata. Plain SHA-256 hashes of private files, private task ids and statements are identity data and never enter the public tree. No optimizer context, prompt or library receives private bytes. Their outcomes reach a promotion decision only in aggregate, and each use is counted. Detailed QA, review, exploit and contamination records of private tasks stay in the private store; the public tree holds only receipts (counts per status and salted commitments). The scan looks for plain identity hashes, private task ids, and every private-file line of at least 40 characters that does not occur in the public tree at the corpus commit; shorter lines and lines shared with the public tree are excluded. It cannot detect paraphrase.

requirements.text: Exploits fail. The verifier restores protected test files and grades outcomes, not paths. Deterministic probes (delete or weaken tests, hard-code outputs, edit the verifier, forge a score file) and an exploit agent told to pass without solving must all fail. A passing exploit rejects the task until it is repaired and QA reruns.

scenarios.then: both blind reviews, both cross-critiques and an adjudication for each disagreement exist, with labels, model ids, versions and hashes, and the blind hashes predate both critiques; a missing artifact, a critique recorded before both blind reviews, or a model review labeled `human` refuses.

requirements.text: Cross adversarial review (OD-4). Each task has two blind review records (statement clarity, solvability, no solution leak, oracle checks outcome, rights): one from Claude in a Claude Code subagent and one from Codex (`codex exec -s read-only` pinned to the corpus commit). Each is labeled `model` with its model id and version, and both hashes are recorded before either reviewer sees the other report. Then each model writes a cross-critique that cites the other report's hash. The owner settles every disagreement in an adjudication record labeled `human`; a majority is not a consensus.

scenarios.given: a synthetic job with injected infra errors
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record: command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits. Planned path: specs/082-harness-task-qa-infra-controls/evidence/t014.json, specs/082-harness-task-qa-infra-controls/evidence/t015-controls.json.
scenarios.then: infra errors are counted apart, excluded from the agent denominator, shown in the bounds, and over the threshold the job is `invalid`; a trial with one infra attempt and a later pass counts once, as a pass; a quota stop over the threshold is `invalid`, and under it `stopped`.

requirements.text: Infrastructure errors kept separate. A trial outcome is one of `pass`, `fail`, `infra-error` (closed subclasses: setup, provider, quota-stop, runtime-crash, verifier-crash, config-drift) or `not-attempted`. Classification follows a rule frozen before data. An infra error never counts as 0 or as a pass; it leaves the agent-outcome denominator, is reported with its count, and bounds the rate both ways. An agent that exceeds its registered time budget is a `fail`. Reruns use fresh run ids and are all kept; the job validity threshold is OD-5. Accounting, frozen before data: the unit is the registered trial; a trial has at most three attempts (the first and two reruns); its outcome is that of its first attempt that is not an infra error; it is an `infra-error` only when every attempt is, with the last attempt's subclass. The OD-5 threshold divides infra-error trials by registered trials. Precedence: a job over the threshold, or with a task that lost all its trials, is `invalid` whatever else stopped it; otherwise a quota stop leaves the remaining trials `not-attempted` and the job `stopped`, which SPEC-083 reports as `inconclusive`.

requirements.text: Pinned and recorded configuration. Each trial records requested and observed model id, reasoning effort, host and agent versions, CPU, memory, disk, timeout, network policy and image digest when used. A mismatch is config-drift.

scenarios.given: a trial whose run id is already registered, or a result whose bytes match an earlier run's
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record: command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits. Planned path: specs/082-harness-task-qa-infra-controls/evidence/t014.json.
scenarios.then: it refuses; two independent trials with byte-identical score files are both accepted.

requirements.text: Fresh run ids, no cache reuse. Each trial has a new run id from a register, a fresh workspace and no reused result, session or cache (the SWE-bench `run_id` hazard). Reuse is detected by provenance, not by byte equality: at start the register issues a nonce to the trial, and the result record carries the run id, workspace id and nonce. The workspace path has never been used, and host and session caches are empty at start, which is recorded. Independent trials may produce identical result bytes.

requirements.text: Contamination record. Each task carries a canary id and records its public source date against each model's stated knowledge cutoff. Reports say the canary is a detection aid and not a guarantee; no task is called contamination-free.

requirements.text: No authority and handoff. The frozen corpus manifest is handed to SPEC-083 and SPEC-084 by hash. No record here authorizes execution. A SPEC-083 regression verdict needs at least 20 `qa-passed` tasks in `private-holdout`, a feasibility target separate from H1 (owner, 2026-11-24). Under OD-1 and OD-7 the first corpus gives about 4 to 10 such tasks, so SPEC-083 reports `descriptive-only` until later batches of new lineages reach 20; OD-1 and OD-7 are unchanged.

scientific_limits: Engineering formats and procedures; no harness verdict. Tasks from one repository are coupled; inference must count lineages, not tasks. Public source history may be in model pretraining; the private split limits optimizer leakage only. Repeated held-out use leaks through selection. A model reviewer is independent model review, not human review. A Codex review is not human review or approval.
scope: Draft documentation-only specification of the task record, corpus manifest, lineage and partition rules, private held-out split, per-task QA (oracle, no-op, exploit probes, exploit agent, two blind model reviews with owner adjudication), infrastructure-error taxonomy, pinned configuration, fresh run ids and contamination record for harness evaluation. Nothing implemented or run.
